attacks.claim: Open-data export publishes ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, and created_at per poll, publicly under CC-BY. Combined with verified flag and timestamps, these quasi-identifiers allow re-identification of individual residents, and the export is irreversible once published.
attacks.evidence: "one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org with columns ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, verified, created_at. resident_id is removed before export."

attacks.claim: Verified residents' address, zip, birth_year and gender are collected for jury-pool demographic reports and are linked to poll responses via the verified flag and zip/ward, creating a linkable dataset of sensitive personal data that the plan does not justify or protect.
attacks.evidence: "Verified residents already have address, zip, birth_year, gender (collected at optional verification for the jury-pool-style demographic balance reports)."

attacks.claim: Purchasing the county voter file (with mobile numbers) and bulk-SMSing 142,000 registered voters is repurposing government-held personal data for an unrelated civic-app marketing campaign without consent, violating the anonymous-first, opt-in premise.
attacks.evidence: "Purchase the county voter registration file from the County Clerk ($400, includes mobile numbers where provided)." / "send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000)"

attacks.claim: Unsolicited automated SMS to 142,000 people via Twilio, with recurring reminders, likely violates TCPA consent requirements for marketing/automated texts, and voter-file use for commercial or solicitation purposes is typically restricted by state law and the Clerk's data-use terms. No legal review is referenced.
attacks.evidence: "send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000) with a link to the first poll, then 3 automated reminders over 10 days." / "Reply STOP handled by Twilio's default opt-out."

attacks.claim: Using a government-run civic poll for advocacy-adjacent public sentiment on council items, with staff-attached polls, and publishing council-staff results may raise lobbying or election-adjacent concerns if the poll is used to influence a decision; no review is specified.
attacks.evidence: "Ward Voice gives residents a direct voice on the items council is actually deciding"

attacks.claim: Unverified responses are accepted with self-selected ward and rate limiting by device fingerprint and IP, which are trivially bypassed; the 'queued for review' path is unspecified and the anti-brigading guarantee rests on the separation of tallies alone.
attacks.evidence: "1 response per poll per device fingerprint + 1 per verified resident; unverified responses over 3/min from one IP are queued for review."

attacks.claim: The plan's own survey shows only 9% wanted polls, yet the plan makes polls the centerpiece; the stated problem-solution fit is unsupported and the 30%-new-users metric is tied to a mass SMS campaign rather than value.
attacks.evidence: "Polls on upcoming items — 9%" / "Ward Voice ... is the centerpiece of the FY27 roadmap."

attacks.claim: Success metrics (6,000 responses, 30% new users) have no baseline or justification, and the 1,240-person survey with kiosk and in-app sampling is not representative of the city; the 9% figure contradicts the centerpiece framing without acknowledgment.
attacks.evidence: "6,000 poll responses in the first 30 days." / "30% of responses from residents not previously active on OurTown."

attacks.claim: Staff cannot edit or delete responses and the open-data export is public and weekly; there is no retraction or takedown path for erroneous, abusive, or personal content submitted in free text or re-identifiable records.

The launch SMS blast to 142,000 numbers in one week with 5k concurrency load test has no rate-limit, Twilio cost ceiling, or failure handling for carrier throttling and bounce/error rates; a bug in the reminder schedule could resend repeatedly.
attacks.evidence: "then 3 automated reminders over 10 days" / "load test (target 5k concurrent)"

attacks.claim: SMS cost for ~142,000 messages plus 3 reminders (~570,000 messages) is not budgeted; only the $400 file purchase is stated.
attacks.evidence: "Purchase the county voter registration file from the County Clerk ($400"

attacks.claim: Ranking UI is specified as drag or tap-to-rank with no keyboard, screen-reader, or motion-alternative requirement beyond a generic 'accessibility pass' in week 5.
Twilio is a single third-party SMS provider and the voter file is a vendor-handed dataset; exit cost and data-residency for phone numbers are unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: "Load numbers into Twilio and send an automated SMS"

attacks.claim: The week-4 scope bundles voter-file import, SMS pipeline, open-data export and staff PDF into one week with no testing plan for the export anonymization.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: open-data export, staff PDF, voter-file import + SMS pipeline."
